name: UDR (Unified Demonstration Retriever for In-Context Learning)
venue: ACL 2023 (Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 4644-4668)
authors_affiliation: Xiaonan Li, Kai Lv, Hang Yan, Tianyang Lin, Wei Zhu, Yuan Ni, Guotong Xie, Xiaoling Wang, Xipeng Qiu. Primary affiliation: Fudan University (Shanghai Key Laboratory of Intelligent Information Processing / School of Computer Science); also East China Normal University and Pingan Health Tech. Corresponding authors: Hang Yan / Tianyang Lin and Xipeng Qiu.
task_domain: NLP in-context learning (ICL) demonstration retrieval spanning classification, multi-choice, NLI, semantic parsing, summarization, code summarization, data-to-text, text simplification, story/commonsense generation; QA-style and generation tasks. Not agent/planning/tool-use.
problem_setting: Offline, single-turn (non-interactive) in-context learning: given a test input x_test, retrieve a few relevant labeled (input,output) demonstrations from an annotated training set D_train of the same task so a frozen inference LM conditions on them and directly outputs the prediction. Supervision is available as ground-truth training labels, and the training signal is the inference LM's feedback (conditional likelihood of the gold output given a candidate demonstration). Single-agent, no environment interaction. The goal is a SINGLE multi-task retriever covering 30+ tasks instead of one task-specific retriever per task.
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (labeled input-output example pairs {x', y'}) drawn from the task's training set.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the (frozen) annotated training set of each task serves as the demonstration pool indexed with FAISS at inference time. No growing/episodic memory written during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective: retriever ranks training examples by learned similarity and selects the top demonstrations (k determined by LM context budget for generation tasks, fixed k=8 for classification/multi-choice). The training objective is list-wise ranking (LambdaRank-style) over candidates, not minimal-set completeness or precision-driven variable-size selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve only (Reuse=verbatim ICL exemplar injection but no explicit case adaptation; no Revise; no Retain). Effective flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: partial/verbatim, Revise: no, Retain: no]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as demonstration retrieval for in-context learning and list-wise ranking from LM feedback; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner or frame itself as case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (a problem-solution / input-output example pair) from the training set.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: each task's training set is encoded offline by the demonstration encoder E_d after training; candidates for training are mined iteratively offline (BM25/Elasticsearch initialization then retriever-self-mining). No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index per task (FAISS over the task's training-set embeddings). Task identity is handled by prepending a task instruction to each example before encoding (context/metadata-keyed) rather than a separate structural index; each task has its own flat index searched at inference.
retriever_type: Learned dense bi-encoder (DPR-style, two BERT-base-uncased encoders E_q and E_d with CLS pooling); single multi-task model. BM25 (Elasticsearch) is used only to initialize candidates during training.
retriever_learning_signal: LM-feedback / downstream-task-effectiveness ranking. Candidates are scored by the inference LM's likelihood of the gold output conditioned on the candidate demonstration (s_gen = p_G(y|z,x) for generation; s_cls = normalized p_G(y|z,x) over the label set for classification), then ranked, and the retriever is trained with a list-wise LambdaRank-inspired pairwise ranking loss plus an in-batch (InfoNCE-style) negative loss. Trained multi-task across all tasks. Not contrastive on surface-similarity labels; not RL.
query_construction: Raw test input x prepended with the task's short natural-language task instruction I_i (e.g., 'Summarize the text'), encoded by query encoder E_q(I_i ⊕ x). Demonstration keys are encoded as E_d(I_i ⊕ z). No query decomposition or expansion.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: the query is the single test input formed once before answering; retrieval happens once per test example.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per test input before the inference LM generates the answer.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (always retrieve once per test example before inference). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No separate reranking stage at inference (single dense bi-encoder retrieval). During TRAINING, an iterative candidate-mining loop effectively re-ranks/re-mines candidates with the updated retriever each iteration, but the deployed inference pipeline is single-stage FAISS top-k.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond ordering: retrieved demonstrations are concatenated into the prompt (ascendingly sorted by similarity, most similar nearest to the test input). No decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools; for demonstrations, each example/key is augmented with a short task-instruction prefix before embedding, but no synthetic-query/summary expansion).
index_content_separation: N/A (no progressive disclosure / index-then-content separation; full demonstrations are both indexed and injected).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or external protocol; static per-task FAISS index).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools / no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-L retrieved demonstrations are concatenated with the test input and fed to a frozen inference LM which decodes the output greedily (G([z_1; z_2; ...; z_L; x_test])). Demonstrations are used verbatim as ICL exemplars; the retriever (not the LM) is what is trained.
planning_integration: N/A for planning/acting; one-shot exemplars at inference time. Retrieval is decoupled from any planning loop: retrieve-then-generate in a single forward pass.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: one retrieval per test input, demonstrations injected once before a single LM generation. No per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar (retrieved demonstrations used as-is in the prompt); no LLM-prompted adaptation or execution-feedback revision of the retrieved case.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw labeled example pairs (input-output demonstrations) injected verbatim as text into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw labeled training example); lowest abstraction level, no distilled strategy/guideline/workflow/skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware/effectiveness-aware training: training on LM-feedback list-wise ranking with iterative hard-negative mining teaches the retriever to down-rank unhelpful candidates, improving the quality (helpfulness) of retrieved demonstrations. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module at inference. The paper also reports robustness to demonstration ordering (high-quality demonstrations are order-insensitive, gap within ~1 point).
memory_type: none (static training-set index; no episodic/skill/workflow memory).
write_back: False. No new experiences/cases are stored back into a memory during deployment; the retrievable store is the fixed training set encoded offline.
online_growth: False. The index is frozen after offline training/encoding; it does not grow at test time.
failure_experience_usage: No stored failure memory at deployment. During TRAINING, low-scoring mined candidates act as hard negatives (contrastive negative signal) in the list-wise ranking loss, so negative/less-helpful examples shape the retriever, but they are not retrieved/stored as failure experiences for the agent.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only at most during offline candidate mining (each training iteration re-mines candidates with the updated retriever); no deployment-time mutation of stored entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: the retriever is a LEARNED ranking model trained from LM feedback (list-wise LambdaRank loss), so selection is learned rather than fixed similarity top-k. However it is not an RL/value-based sequential policy (no MDP, no soft Q-learning); at inference it reduces to learned-similarity top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single shared multi-task retriever across 30+ tasks (one model serves all tasks instead of per-task retrievers), but it is not multi-agent experience sharing; no cross-agent memory.
benchmarks: 30+ tasks across 13 task families: Sentiment Classification (SST-2, SST-5, Amazon, Yelp, MR, CR); Topic Classification (AGNews, Yahoo, TREC, DBPedia); Multi-Choice (COPA, Cosmos QA, ComE, ComV); NLI (MNLI, SNLI, RTE); Subjectivity (Subj); Linguistic Acceptability (COLA); Semantic Parsing (BREAK, MTOP, SMCalFlow); Text Summarization (CNN/DailyMail, PubMed, Reddit); Commonsense Generation (CommonGen); Story Generation (RocStory, Roc Ending); Code Summarization (Go, Python, Java, PHP); Text Simplification (WikiAuto, Turk, ASSET); Data-to-Text (DART, E2E). Unseen-dataset evaluation: Twitter sentiment, QNLI, Ruby and JavaScript code summarization.
benchmark_family: QA / NLU+NLG ICL task suite (classification, multi-choice, NLI, semantic parsing, summarization, code, data-to-text). Not in the standard web/embodied/tool/SWE/memory benchmark families; closest to a broad multi-task NLP ICL benchmark family.
baselines: Random, BM25 (Elasticsearch/off-the-shelf), SBERT (Sentence-BERT paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2), Instructor (instruction-tuned text embedder, base size), DR-Target (task-specific target-similarity retriever trained with DPR using BM25 target-similarity positives), and EPR (Efficient Prompt Retriever, Rubin et al. 2022) trained per-task with the same hyper-parameters. Single-task UDR is also compared in ablations.
key_metrics: Per-task task-specific metrics (accuracy for classification/multi-choice/NLI; task metrics such as exact-match/structured-match for semantic parsing, ROUGE for summarization, BLEU/CIDEr-style metrics for generation, SARI for simplification, code-summarization metrics, etc. - exact per-task metrics listed in the paper's Appendix A), reported as task scores and per-family / overall averages. Headline comparison is the overall average task score across families.
headline_result: A single UDR model outperforms all baselines across 30+ tasks. Overall averages (GPT-Neo-2.7B as scoring+inference LM): on classification/multi-choice tasks UDR reaches 73.2 overall vs EPR 68.8, Instructor 63.2, SBERT 61.6, BM25 57.7, Random 47.3; on generation tasks UDR reaches 30.9 overall vs EPR 27.7, Instructor/BM25 24.2, SBERT 23.7, Random 15.8. UDR improves over the strongest prior task-specific retriever EPR by ~4.4 (classification) and ~3.2 (generation) average points while using a single multi-task model.
ablations: Table 3 ablation on SMCalFlow / SST-2 / Java (avg in parentheses): full UDR 60.8/91.3/23.2 (58.4); -w/o Task Prompt 60.1/90.8/21.9 (57.6, small drop -> task instructions help distinguish tasks); -w/o MultiTask 60.9/91.0/22.9 (58.3, single-task UDR nearly matches full -> multi-task sharing gives small gains and single-task UDR still beats EPR); -w/o Rank Loss 56.7/89.2/21.1 (55.7, largest drop -> list-wise ranking from LM feedback is the key driver); -w/o Self-Guided 59.5/90.2/19.7 (56.5 -> iterative candidate mining is important, especially for generation/code). Additional analyses: transferability across inference LMs (1.3B-175B, Table 4), unseen-dataset zero-shot transfer (Table 5), demonstration ordering robustness (Table 6), and demonstration-quantity effect (Figure 3, UDR with 2 demos beats BM25/EPR with 8).
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end downstream task metrics (ICL task scores) are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics like Recall@k / nDCG are not reported separately. Retrieval quality is measured indirectly through downstream ICL performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome only: final ICL task performance is scored; no intermediate process/faithfulness or step-wise retrieval metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Parameter/deployment efficiency is the central efficiency argument: one shared UDR model replaces N task-specific retrievers, reducing parameter-storage and deployment cost as tasks scale. Training efficiency: Elasticsearch/BM25 used to initialize candidates and FAISS for fast inference search; iterative mining adds 3 training iterations (iter0/1/2). Demonstration-quantity analysis shows UDR with 2 demonstrations beats BM25/EPR with 8, i.e., fewer, higher-quality demos lower token cost. No explicit API-cost/latency numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed/budget-capped: for generation tasks the number of demonstrations L is set by the inference LM's max input length C (sum of demo lengths + |x_test| + reserved |y| <= C); for classification and multi-choice tasks L is fixed to 8 (increasing L gives negligible gains). Demonstrations are ascendingly sorted by similarity (most similar closest to the test input).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; uses 30+ existing public datasets across 13 task families). [uncertain on exact per-dataset sizes - listed in paper Appendix A which was not fully extracted].
builds_on: EPR / Efficient Prompt Retriever (Rubin et al., 2022) for LM-feedback demonstration retrieval and its binary positive/negative training; DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020) bi-encoder architecture; BERT-base-uncased encoders (Devlin et al., 2019); LambdaRank (Burges, 2010) for the list-wise ranking loss; FAISS (Johnson et al., 2021) for inference search; GPT-Neo (Black et al., 2021) as scoring/inference LM; KATE/KNN demonstration selection (Liu et al., 2022) and Shi et al. (2022) cross-lingual retrievers as the demonstration-retrieval line.
contrasts_with: EPR (Rubin et al., 2022) - task-specific, binary LM-feedback labels, manually-limited candidate range; off-the-shelf retrievers BM25 and SBERT (heuristic, no task supervision); Instructor (instruction-tuned embedder); DR-Target (task-specific target-similarity retriever); per-task task-specialized retrievers (Das et al. 2021 KBQA, Hu et al. 2022 dialogue state tracking, Poesia et al. 2022). UDR contrasts by being a single multi-task retriever with list-wise ranking and iterative full-dataset candidate mining.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval): a direct generalization of the LM-feedback demonstration-retrieval line (EPR -> UDR), moving from per-task binary-label retrievers to a single multi-task list-wise-ranking retriever; predecessor to later unified/retrieval-based ICL retrievers (e.g., RUIE 2024 for unified information extraction) that cite UDR.
